key_insight: ImageNet-pretrained MobileNet with differential attention performed best (AUC 0.862 ± 0.005), while adding spatial attention to channel attention showed no detectable benefit.
clinical_relevance: Distinguishing high- from low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma matters for prognosis and treatment, but these research results do not establish clinical readiness.
method: Compared CNN attention variants, pretrained MobileNet, and a Phikon foundation-model benchmark.
Used stain normalization, slide-level pooling, and five-fold slide-grouped cross-validation.
Repeated training across three seeds and applied statistical comparisons with multiple-testing correction.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included 259 UBC-OCEAN whole-slide images (217 high-grade, 42 low-grade), with slide-grouped splits designed to prevent slide-information leakage.
watch_item: A colour-only classifier achieved AUC 0.66, raising concern that stain-related signals could limit generalization across laboratories.
paper_title: Which Attention Helps? A Slide-Level Ablation of Attention-Augmented CNNs for Serous Ovarian Carcinoma Grading
